newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $66, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $66, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle were bid $66.00 per cwt, steady with last week's top, but the bids were passed by owners pricing cattle at $69.00 to $70.00, feedlot sources said.
Fed cattle prices were underpinned by strong beef prices, tight supplies of finished cattle and weather, they said.

Feedlots pricing cattle at $70.00 were in northwest Kansas, which received 10 to 12 inches of snow on Monday, sources said. Southwest Kansas got up to four inches of snow, but could get more by the end of the day. The heavy snow could affect cattle performance, sources there said.
Snowfall also was expected in the Texas Panhandle by Wednesday, with local forecasters calling for four to six inches, one feedlot manager in the Panhandle said.
Packer buyers were calling early with bids trying to line up sales, but several cattle feeders said it would take a bid of at least $68.00 to buy cattle.
Beef prices on Monday were quoted $1.26 to $2.37 per cwt higher on 157 fabricated loads sold, USDA said.
Heavier-choice beef was quoted up $1.81 at $101.26, a gain of $5.65 in the last week, USDA statistics showed.
